task.title: Set the time, day, and date on a Seiko 4R36 watch
task.shortdesc: Set the time, day of the week, and numerical date after the watch has stopped or displays incorrect calendar information.

context.p: The Seiko 4R36 movement displays the time, numerical date, and day of the week. The date changes around midnight, while the day display completes its change later.
context.note: Do not use the quick-set day or date function between 9:00 p.m. and 4:00 a.m. Doing so may prevent the calendar from changing correctly or may damage the mechanism.

ul.li: Confirm that the watch is operating.
Use an accurate time and date reference.
If the watch has a screw-down crown, unlock the crown before beginning the procedure.

step.cmd: Pull the crown out to the first click.
Turn the crown counterclockwise until the previous day’s numerical date appears.
step.info: For example, if the current date is July 19, set the date display to 18.

step.cmd: Turn the crown clockwise until the previous day of the week appears.
step.info: If the watch has a bilingual day display, select the preferred language.

step.cmd: Pull the crown out to the second click when the seconds hand reaches the 12 o’clock position.
Turn the crown to advance the hands until the day and date change to the current day and date.
step.info: The calendar change identifies the midnight transition and helps establish the correct a.m. or p.m. setting.

step.cmd: Continue turning the crown to set the current time.
Push the crown back to its normal position in synchronization with an accurate time signal.
If applicable, press and turn the screw-down crown clockwise until it is secured.

result.p: The watch displays the correct time, day, and date, and the crown is returned to its normal secured position.

postreq.p: Observe the watch through the next calendar transition to verify that the day and date advance correctly.
